description: MCP Servers settings tab within the runner Settings panel. Allows users to configure external Model Context Protocol servers that extend the runner's capabilities with additional tools. Supports two transport types: stdio (subprocess) and HTTP. Each server can be connected/disconnected on demand, and when connected its tools are listed and become available as workflow steps. The tab manages the full server lifecycle: list (with connection status), create, update, delete, connect, disconnect, and tool discovery. Server configurations are stored in the runner's PostgreSQL database via Tauri IPC commands (list_mcp_servers, create_mcp_server, update_mcp_server, delete_mcp_server, connect_mcp_server, disconnect_mcp_server, get_mcp_servers_status).

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The MCP Servers tab renders a SectionHeader with title 'MCP Servers' and a description. Below it is a 'Configured Servers' subsection with an 'Add Server' button. At the bottom is a 'What is MCP?' info box. The form and delete confirmation modal overlay the list when active.

assertions.description: An h3 heading with text 'MCP Servers' is present as the section title
A description paragraph reading 'Configure external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that the runner can call to extend its capabilities.' is visible below the heading

criteria.textContent: Configure external MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers

assertions.description: A subheading 'Configured Servers' is present above the server list area
A 'What is MCP?' info box is present at the bottom of the page, containing an explanation of the Model Context Protocol

groups.name: Add Server Button
groups.description: The 'Add Server' button appears in the header row of the Configured Servers section. Clicking it shows the add form. The button is always visible regardless of how many servers exist.

assertions.description: An 'Add Server' button is present in the Configured Servers section header row

Clicking the 'Add Server' button reveals the add server form with blank fields (name, description, transport=HTTP by default, url, headers, timeout=30, enabled=true, autoStart=false). The server list area is replaced by the form. The form title reads 'Add New Server' and the submit button reads 'Create'.

groups.name: Empty State — No Servers
groups.description: When no MCP servers have been configured, the server list area shows an empty state with a message and hint text. This is the initial state for a fresh runner installation.

assertions.description: When no servers are configured, the text 'No MCP servers configured' is displayed in the list area
assertions.precondition: No MCP servers have been added

assertions.description: Below the empty state message, hint text 'Add a server to extend runner capabilities' is displayed

criteria.textContent: Add a server to extend runner capabilities

assertions.precondition: No MCP servers have been added

assertions.description: While the initial list_mcp_servers Tauri command is in flight, a loading spinner is shown in place of the server list. Once the command returns, the spinner is replaced by either the empty state or the server cards. No error state is displayed for load failures — errors are silently logged.
assertions.precondition: MCP Servers tab has just been navigated to

groups.name: Server Card Structure
groups.description: Each configured server renders as a card with a header row containing expand/collapse toggle, transport icon, server name, status badges, endpoint text, connection status indicator, and three action buttons (connect/disconnect, edit, delete). Cards can be expanded to reveal the available tools list.

assertions.description: Each server card displays the server name with data-content-label='server name'
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is configured

assertions.description: Each server card displays the server endpoint (command for stdio, URL for HTTP) with data-content-label='server endpoint'
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is configured

assertions.description: Each server card header row shows: (1) a chevron icon for expand/collapse, (2) a transport icon (Terminal for stdio, Globe for HTTP), (3) the server name in bold, (4) optional 'Disabled' badge in gray if enabled=false, (5) optional 'Auto-start' badge in blue if autoStart=true, (6) the endpoint text (command or URL) in muted style, (7) a colored connection status indicator dot with text label, (8) connect/disconnect Power icon button, (9) Edit pencil icon button, (10) Delete trash icon button. The order is fixed and all elements are always present when a server exists.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is configured

groups.name: Connection Status Indicators
groups.description: Each server card shows a colored connection status indicator with three possible states: Connected (green pulsing dot), Error (red dot), or Disconnected (gray dot). The status is fetched via get_mcp_servers_status on mount and after each connect/disconnect operation.

assertions.description: When a server is connected, a status indicator with data-content-label='server connected' and text 'Connected' is shown on its card
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is in the connected state

assertions.description: When a server connection has failed, a status indicator with data-content-label='server error' and text 'Error' is shown. The element has a title tooltip containing the error message from the backend.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server has a connection error

assertions.description: When a server is not connected, a status indicator with data-content-label='server disconnected' and text 'Disconnected' is shown on its card
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is in the disconnected state

assertions.description: Connection status is determined by the McpServerStatus object returned by get_mcp_servers_status, keyed by server ID. A server with status.connected=true shows the connected state. A server with connected=false and status.error present shows the error state with the error in the tooltip. A server with connected=false and no error shows disconnected. A server ID absent from the status map also shows disconnected. Status is refreshed after every connect/disconnect action but is NOT polled continuously.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is configured

groups.name: Server Status Badges
groups.description: Server cards optionally show 'Disabled' and 'Auto-start' badges in the header row. These reflect the server's enabled and autoStart configuration fields.

assertions.description: A 'Disabled' badge in gray styling appears on a server card when that server's enabled field is false. No badge appears when enabled is true.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server has enabled=false

assertions.description: An 'Auto-start' badge in blue styling appears on a server card when that server's autoStart field is true
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server has autoStart=true

assertions.description: When a server has enabled=false, its Connect/Disconnect button (Power icon) is disabled — it cannot be connected while disabled. The 'Disabled' badge visually signals this restriction. When enabled=true and autoStart=true, the 'Auto-start' badge indicates the runner will attempt to connect to this server automatically at launch without any manual connect action.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server has enabled=false

groups.name: Connect / Disconnect Actions
groups.description: Each server card has a connect/disconnect button (Power icon). When a server is disconnected or in error state, clicking it calls connect_mcp_server. When connected, clicking it calls disconnect_mcp_server. During the operation a spinning RefreshCw icon replaces the Power icon and the button is disabled.

assertions.description: Clicking the Connect button (Power icon) on a disconnected server shows a spinning RefreshCw icon during the operation, invokes connect_mcp_server with the server ID, and on success the connection status changes to 'Connected' and the tools list becomes available when the card is expanded. On failure, the status shows 'Error' with the error message as a tooltip.

target.label: Connect button on disconnected server card

assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is in the disconnected state

assertions.description: Clicking the Disconnect button (PowerOff icon) on a connected server shows a spinning RefreshCw icon, invokes disconnect_mcp_server with the server ID, and on success the status changes to 'Disconnected'. The tools list (if expanded) becomes empty showing 'Connect to see available tools'.

target.label: Disconnect button on connected server card

assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is in the connected state

assertions.description: The Connect button is disabled (not clickable) when the server's enabled field is false. The 'Disabled' badge on the card is the visual indicator that the Connect button will not respond to clicks. To connect a disabled server, the user must first edit it and set enabled=true.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server has enabled=false

groups.name: Expanded Server Tools List
groups.description: Clicking the chevron button on a server card expands it to reveal a tools grid. Each tool shows a Wrench icon, the tool name in monospace with data-content-label='tool name', and an optional description. If connected but no tools exist, shows 'No tools available'. If disconnected, shows 'Connect to see available tools'. If in error state, shows the error message.

assertions.description: The expanded section header shows a tool count with data-content-label='available tools count'. The format shows the number of available tools.
assertions.precondition: A server card is expanded and the server is connected

assertions.description: Each tool in the tools grid displays its name in monospace font with data-content-label='tool name'
assertions.precondition: A server card is expanded, the server is connected, and it exposes at least one tool

assertions.description: When a server card is expanded but the server is in the disconnected state, the tools section shows the text 'Connect to see available tools' rather than a tool grid
assertions.precondition: A server card is expanded and the server is in the disconnected state

assertions.description: The tools listed in the expanded card come directly from the McpToolInfo array returned by connect_mcp_server. Each tool has a name (string), an optional description (string), and an inputSchema (JSON schema for parameters). The tools are the server's published MCP capabilities — what the runner can invoke when the server is connected. These tool names become usable as workflow step identifiers. An empty tools list from a connected server is valid and means the server exposes no callable tools.
assertions.precondition: A server card is expanded and the server is connected

groups.name: Add / Edit Form Structure
groups.description: The add/edit form replaces the server list when active. It contains: title ('Add New Server' or 'Edit Server'), Name (required), Description (optional), transport selection (Stdio / HTTP radio cards), transport-specific fields, and common settings (timeout, enabled, auto-start). Actions are Cancel and Create/Update.

assertions.description: A text input labeled 'Name' with placeholder 'My MCP Server' is present in the form. The field is marked required.
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

assertions.description: Two transport option cards are shown: 'Stdio' (with Terminal icon and description 'Run as subprocess') and 'HTTP' (with Globe icon and description 'Connect to server'). These act as radio buttons — exactly one is selected at a time, highlighted with a primary border.
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

assertions.description: A 'Cancel' button is present in the form action row. Clicking it hides the form and returns to the server list without saving any changes.
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

assertions.description: A submit button labeled 'Create' (for new servers) or 'Update' (for editing) is present. The button is disabled when the Name field is empty or while a save is in progress. During saving, the button text changes to 'Saving...'.
assertions.precondition: The add form is visible with the Name field filled

groups.name: Transport-Specific Fields
groups.description: The form shows different fields depending on the selected transport type. Stdio shows Command, Arguments, and Working Directory. HTTP shows Server URL and Headers. Switching transport hides the previous transport's fields. A warning banner appears when Stdio is selected.

assertions.description: When HTTP transport is selected, a 'Server URL' text input appears in monospace with placeholder 'http://localhost:3000'
assertions.precondition: The form is visible and HTTP transport is selected

assertions.description: When Stdio transport is selected, a 'Command' text input appears in monospace with placeholder 'npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem'
assertions.precondition: The form is visible and Stdio transport is selected

assertions.description: When Stdio transport is selected, an amber/yellow warning banner appears reading 'Note: Stdio transport is not yet fully implemented. HTTP is recommended.'

criteria.textContent: Stdio transport is not yet fully implemented

assertions.precondition: The form is visible and Stdio transport is selected

assertions.description: Clicking the Stdio transport card hides the HTTP fields (Server URL, Headers) and shows the Stdio fields (Command, Arguments, Working Directory) plus the Stdio warning banner. Clicking the HTTP card hides the Stdio fields and shows the HTTP fields. Previously entered values in hidden fields are preserved in component state but not visible.
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

groups.name: Form Common Settings
groups.description: Below the transport-specific fields, the form shows three settings that apply to both transport types: Timeout (number input, 1-300 seconds), Enabled checkbox, and Auto-start checkbox. These settings are always visible regardless of transport selection.

assertions.description: A 'Timeout' number input labeled in seconds is present, accepting values between 1 and 300, with a default of 30
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

assertions.description: An 'Enabled' checkbox with description 'Server can be connected' is present. When checked (default), the server can be connected. When unchecked, the 'Disabled' badge appears on the card and the Connect button is inactive.
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

assertions.description: An 'Auto-start' checkbox with description 'Connect automatically when runner launches' is present
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible

groups.name: Form Create and Update Behavior
groups.description: Submitting the form calls create_mcp_server (new) or update_mcp_server (edit). On success, the form closes and the server list refreshes. The form processes arguments (split by newline) and headers (JSON or key:value lines) before sending to the backend.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Create' with a valid name submits the form via the create_mcp_server Tauri command. The button shows 'Saving...' during the request. On success, the form is hidden, the server list refreshes showing the new server card, and the new server's status is 'Disconnected'. On error, the form stays open and an error is logged.
assertions.precondition: The add form is visible with a valid server name entered

assertions.description: Clicking 'Update' submits changes to the existing server via update_mcp_server. The backend kills any active stdio subprocess for the server before applying the update. On success, the form closes, the server list refreshes with the updated values, and the server's connection status is reset to 'Disconnected' (since the subprocess was killed).
assertions.precondition: The edit form is visible with changes made

assertions.description: The Headers textarea (HTTP transport) accepts input in two formats: (1) JSON object: '{"Authorization": "Bearer token"}' parsed via JSON.parse, or (2) key: value lines one per line. The form attempts JSON.parse first; if it fails, falls back to splitting lines on ':' and trimming. Invalid lines are silently skipped. The resulting Record<string, string> is sent to the backend. The Arguments textarea (stdio transport) is split on newline and empty lines are filtered out, resulting in a string[] sent as the args field.
assertions.precondition: The add or edit form is visible with HTTP transport selected

groups.name: Edit Server Flow
groups.description: Clicking the Edit (pencil) button on a server card populates the form with the server's existing values and shows it in edit mode. The form title reads 'Edit Server' and the submit button reads 'Update'.

assertions.description: Clicking the Edit (pencil icon) button on a server card opens the form with fields pre-populated: name, description, transport, command/args/cwd or url/headers, timeout_seconds, enabled, autoStart. The form title is 'Edit Server' and the submit button text is 'Update'. The form replaces the server list.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is configured

assertions.description: When the edit form is open, the form title reads 'Edit Server'
assertions.precondition: The edit form is open for an existing server

groups.name: Delete Confirmation Modal
groups.description: Clicking the Delete (trash) button on a server card opens a confirmation modal with a dark overlay. The modal shows a title 'Delete Server', a message naming the server being deleted, and two buttons: Cancel and Delete (red).

assertions.description: When the delete confirmation is open, a modal with title 'Delete Server' appears over a dark overlay
assertions.precondition: A server delete button has been clicked

assertions.description: The delete confirmation modal shows a message in the format 'Are you sure you want to delete "<serverName>"? This cannot be undone.' where <serverName> is the actual name of the server being deleted
assertions.precondition: A server delete button has been clicked

assertions.description: Clicking the red 'Delete' button in the confirmation modal invokes delete_mcp_server with the server ID. The backend kills any active subprocess for the server before deleting its database record. On success, the modal closes and the server list refreshes with the server removed. Clicking 'Cancel' closes the modal without deleting.
assertions.precondition: The delete confirmation modal is open

groups.name: What is MCP Info Box
groups.description: A light-blue info box at the bottom of the tab explains the Model Context Protocol to users who may not be familiar with it.

assertions.description: The info box contains a bold heading 'What is MCP?'

The info box body contains the text: 'The Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows the runner to call external tools and services. You can add MCP servers for databases, file systems, APIs, or custom tools. When connected, their tools become available as workflow steps.'

criteria.textContent: When connected, their tools become available as workflow steps.

groups.name: MCP Server Data Model
groups.description: McpServerConfig is the canonical data structure for a configured MCP server. It is stored in the runner's PostgreSQL database and returned by list_mcp_servers and create/update commands. Understanding this model is essential for verifying that form submissions, CRUD operations, and status displays are correct.

assertions.description: Each McpServerConfig has: id (UUID string), name (string, required), description (optional string), transport ('stdio' | 'http'), command (optional, stdio only), args (optional string[], stdio only), cwd (optional string, stdio only), env (optional Record<string, string>, stdio only), url (optional string, HTTP only), headers (optional Record<string, string>, HTTP only), enabled (boolean), autoStart (boolean), timeout_seconds (number), created_at (ISO timestamp), updated_at (ISO timestamp). When transport is 'stdio', url/headers must be absent. When transport is 'http', command/args/cwd/env must be absent.
assertions.precondition: At least one MCP server is configured

assertions.description: McpToolInfo represents a tool exposed by a connected server and has: name (string, the callable tool identifier), description (optional string, human explanation), inputSchema (JSON schema object describing parameters). Tool names are the identifiers used when invoking tools in workflow steps. The tools are authoritative — they come directly from the MCP server's capabilities response on connection.
assertions.precondition: A server is connected and has at least one tool

assertions.description: Server configurations persist in the runner's PostgreSQL database and survive runner restarts. The runner fetches the full server list on mount via list_mcp_servers. Connection state (connected/disconnected) is NOT persisted — on restart all servers begin disconnected, unless autoStart=true triggers automatic reconnection at startup. The status returned by get_mcp_servers_status reflects live in-memory connection state managed by the MCP client manager, not a database field.
